L1·N5378unmasked layer
Mostly an inhibitory neuron: it is driven strongly negative by the paragraph-break token (`\n`, or a list-marker `#`) that directly follows a boilerplate closing line (e.g. "Thanks for subscribing!", "we'll be happy to assist you!"), while its small positive activations occur on capitalized words that open a new web-page metadata/boilerplate segment ("Posted", "Categories", "Examples", "You", "can").

L18·N1297unmasked layer
This neuron weakly marks clause/phrase-break or pivot points — a token that closes or turns a segment (comma before a contrastive "but", "!" ending an exclamation, a digit ending a number, the head noun starting a new list) — while being strongly suppressed on function words (prepositions/determiners/conjunctions like "during", "the", "in", "or") that continue a phrase smoothly.

L19·N2487unmasked layer
Fires on boundary/segment-break tokens (newlines, em-dashes, the last token of a phrase) right at the point where the text starts to repeat or restate a parallel construction it just used ("Action tag in the front… in the middle", "encode…Parseltongue / decode…Parseltongue", "U.S. Lime Company — X … — Y"); it is a structural position detector rather than a semantic one, and is suppressed on ordinary mid-phrase function words/numerals.
